Setback rules: yards, planes and everything that keeps a building back

Source: R/setbacks.R
yard.Rd

Every rule that keeps a building a distance from a boundary, from a simple yard to a recession plane, a sky exposure plane or a setback proportional to height, is held as a setback: a required distance from an origin line as a function of height, \(d(h)\). The engine takes, for each boundary at each storey, the largest distance any applicable rule requires.

Usage

yard(
  distance = NULL,
  boundaries,
  from_storey = NULL,
  above_height = NULL,
  origin = "boundary",
  when = NULL,
  variant = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  source = NULL,
  activity_status = NULL,
  value_from = NULL
)

plane(
  angle_deg = NULL,
  start_height,
  boundaries,
  slope = NULL,
  set_in = 0,
  angle_by_bearing = NULL,
  angle_by_orientation = NULL,
  vertical_above = NULL,
  max_setback_above = NULL,
  datum = "boundary",
  origin = "boundary",
  when = NULL,
  variant = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  source = NULL,
  activity_status = NULL
)

upper_level_setback(
  distance,
  boundaries,
  above_height = NULL,
  from_storey = NULL,
  origin = "boundary",
  when = NULL,
  variant = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  source = NULL,
  activity_status = NULL
)

proportional_setback(
  ratio,
  boundaries,
  min = 0,
  max = NULL,
  origin = "boundary",
  when = NULL,
  variant = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  source = NULL,
  activity_status = NULL
)

setback_profile(
  height,
  distance,
  boundaries,
  origin = "boundary",
  when = NULL,
  variant = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  source = NULL,
  activity_status = NULL
)

Arguments

distance

Required distance (m), or a formula string. For setback_profile(), the distances (m) required at each of height.

boundaries

Boundary classes the rule applies to, e.g. "road", "side", "rear". See boundary_classes().

from_storey

Applies only from this storey up (1 = ground).

above_height

Applies only to the part of a building above this height (m).

origin

Line the distance is measured from: "boundary" (default), "road_far_side" (the far side of the road in front, as Japan's road slant line) or "road_centreline".

when

Conditions under which the rule applies, from conditions().

variant

Name of the alternative standard this rule belongs to. Rules of different variants are alternatives, never combined.

name

Optional label for the rule.

source

Citation (plan, chapter, rule number).

activity_status

Optional activity status of the standard.

value_from

Instead of distance, a yard set by what is already there: "existing_front_setback" is the average setback of the dwellings on the neighbouring sites along the street (as the Auckland Unitary Plan's Special Character Areas front yard, D18.6.1.3.1), measured from building outlines (find_existing_front_setbacks()). Where nothing could be measured the rule is reported as not applied, never read as no yard.

angle_deg

Plane angle from horizontal, degrees.

start_height

Height (m) above the origin line where the plane starts.

slope

Alternative to angle_deg: rise per unit of horizontal run (e.g. 2.7 for a 2.7:1 plane).

set_in

Horizontal distance (m) inside the origin line where the plane starts.

angle_by_bearing

Optional: angles that vary with the direction the boundary faces, as a data frame with from_deg, to_deg and angle_deg (bearing of the outward normal, clockwise from north).

angle_by_orientation

Optional: angles at the four cardinal bearings, c(north = , east = , south = , west = ), graded linearly in between (Christchurch's recession plane diagrams work this way).

vertical_above

Height (m) above which the plane turns vertical: the setback stays at its value at this height.

max_setback_above

Optional cap on the plane's setback above a height, by the direction the boundary faces: c(height = , north = , east = , south = , west = ). Above height the lesser of the plane and this setback applies.

datum

Ground the start height is measured from: "boundary" (ground at the boundary, the default), "site" (site mean ground) or "road".

ratio

Distance per metre of height.

min, max

Bounds on the distance (m).

height

For setback_profile(): breakpoints of height (m, ascending). Distances between breakpoints are interpolated; beyond the last they stay at the last.

Value

A list with class plancap_setback.

Details

  • yard(): a fixed distance (or a formula), optionally only from a storey or above a height.

  • plane(): a recession / daylight / height-in-relation-to-boundary plane, rising at an angle from a start height above the origin line.

  • upper_level_setback(): an extra setback for the part of a building above a height (a podium step-back).

  • proportional_setback(): a distance proportional to height, with a minimum and maximum (e.g. Germany's 0.4H, at least 3 m).

  • setback_profile(): any piecewise-linear \(d(h)\), for rules none of the above express.

Use setback_distance() to evaluate one.

Examples

yard(3, "road", source = "Rule 7.1")
#> <setback: yard> on "road"
#>  $ distance:3
#>  $ source  :"Rule 7.1"
plane(angle_deg = 45, start_height = 2.5, boundaries = c("side", "rear"))
#> <setback: plane> on "side" and "rear"
#>  $ angle_deg   :45
#>  $ start_height:2.5
# NYC-style sky exposure plane on wide streets: 5.6 vertical to 1 horizontal
plane(slope = 5.6, start_height = 85 * 0.3048, boundaries = "road")
#> <setback: plane> on "road"
#>  $ angle_deg   :79.9
#>  $ start_height:25.9
proportional_setback(0.4, min = 3, boundaries = c("side", "rear"))
#> <setback: proportional> on "side" and "rear"
#>  $ ratio:0.4
#>  $ min  :3
setback_profile(height = c(0, 3.6, 6.9, 30), distance = c(1, 1, 2, 25.1),
                boundaries = c("side", "rear"))
#> <setback: profile> on "side" and "rear"
#>  $ points:List of 4
#>   ..$ :0 1
#>   ..$ :3.6 1
#>   ..$ :6.9 2
#>   ..$ :30 25.1
